newsitem.title: USA: Seven sue Sikorsky Aircraft for discrimination.
newsitem.headline: Seven sue Sikorsky Aircraft for discrimination.

text.p: Seven black workers have filed a class action suit against Sikorsky Aircraft Corp. alleging the helicopter maker maintained racially discriminatory policies and practices.

The complaint, filed in U.S. District Court in Connecticut, alleges Sikorsky paid the workers lower salaries and limited career advancement "in comparison to their Caucasian counterparts," lawyer Dan Berger said in a telephone interview Friday.

Berger, who negotiated a $172 million settlement on behalf of 1,400 black employees of Texaco last November, said it was too early to tell how much money was involved in the action filed Thursday against Sikorsky, "but it will be in the millions of dollars."
The plaintiffs are currently employees at Sikorsky, a subsidiary of United Technologies, where they have worked for between four and 41 years.
Sikorsky spokesman Bill Tuttle said, "We take our commitment to equal employment opportunity very seriously. As a matter of company of policy, we do not discuss litigation."
